html:
SMTO-EXE-0026 — SMTO needs your choice before it can continue this task

GUID: ed3fd33e-d99f-45ca-bbc0-f12beb9234b6
Slug: resource-reconciliation-pending-user-baseline
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • An earlier job that was using the same files or resources has ended, but SMTO can't tell what it finished. Your next command has not started yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the task, find the recovery card that says the blocking job has ended with an uncertain outcome, and note which job it names. That job used the same files or resources as your next command, so its result matters first.
  2. Check the files or service that earlier job was changing, or open its step and read its output, to see what it actually did. SMTO can't confirm what that job finished, so you are the one who decides whether things look right.
  3. If things look right and Resolve forcefully by terminating job is available, select it and read the warning before you confirm. Changes already made are kept. This clears the earlier job's hold so SMTO can start your saved command.
  4. If you are not sure, or that button isn't available, select Stop to end the task instead. Stopping leaves everything as it is so you can look further before anything else runs.

What success looks like

  • The recovery card disappears and the task continues with your saved command.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start the same command in a new task while this one is waiting; both would act on the same files.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Resource recovery found that every blocking job has ended with an uncertain outcome and released its resource claim, so the run is eligible for a user decision that is not yet made.

What this means

  • The recovery decision view found that current blocker state was eligible for user acceptance of a baseline and presented that choice; displaying it does not accept anything. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The recovery decision view found that current blocker state was eligible for user acceptance of a baseline and presented that choice; displaying it does not accept anything.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current blocker revision, ended-process evidence and presented baseline choice through the owning recovery controls.

How to fix it

  • No corrective action is required for this informational outcome.
  • Inspect the resource_reconciliation_request on the run (blocker_status, details, liveness_state, resource_claim_state, historical_effect_uncertain) and the blocking Gateway job's receipt. Verify the target's current state, then submit an explicit decision through the recovery card; this status never triggers execution on its own.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • An explicit supported decision is persisted for the current state, or the task remains blocked.

What not to do

  • Do not turn this status into an automatic retry or a new execution request.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
